name: TitleWithVisual
summary: Title on top, a large illustration area below. The default layout for most scenes.
useWhen: One main illustration: a plot, a formula, a diagram, a list
avoidWhen: Comparing two things side by side: use TwoColumn
children: One illustration (or one <div> holding several elements)

props.name: title
props.description: Scene title, at most ~8 words

props.name: kicker
props.description: Small label above the title

props.name: at
props.description: Time: seconds, "cue:<phrase from the narration>", "cue:<phrase>@end", or "end-<seconds>"

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of the illustration

name: TwoColumn
summary: Two columns side by side, with an optional title. Exactly two children: left, right.
useWhen: Before/after, right/wrong, two ways of solving
Formula on the left, graph on the right
avoidWhen: Only one illustration: use TitleWithVisual
children: Exactly two elements: left column, right column

props.name: at
props.description: Time: seconds, "cue:<phrase from the narration>", "cue:<phrase>@end", or "end-<seconds>"

props.name: ratio
props.description: Width ratio of the left column

name: FullVisual
summary: The whole frame for one element, centered in the safe area.
useWhen: An opening TitleCard
One formula or a big question on its own
avoidWhen: A scene title is needed: use TitleWithVisual

name: TitleCard
summary: A large title opening the lecture or a part of it, with a small label and a subtitle.
useWhen: The opening scene of the video
Moving on to a new part of the lecture
avoidWhen: A title above an illustration: use the TitleWithVisual layout

props.name: kicker
props.description: Small label above, e.g. "Lesson 3 · Derivatives"

props.name: at
props.description: Time: seconds, "cue:<phrase from the narration>", "cue:<phrase>@end", or "end-<seconds>"

name: BulletReveal
summary: A list of points appearing one by one, optionally numbered, with earlier points dimmed.
useWhen: Listing 2–5 short points
End-of-lesson summary
avoidWhen: More than 5 points or points longer than 12 words: split into several scenes

props.name: items
props.type: string | { text: string; at?: number | string }[]
props.description: The points; each is a string or { text, at }. Supports $…$ for math

props.name: at
props.description: When the first point appears (points without their own `at` follow `gap` apart)

props.name: focus
props.description: Dim earlier points when a new one appears

props.name: effect
props.description: How each point appears

name: Formula
summary: Shows a math formula (LaTeX via KaTeX) with an entrance effect.
useWhen: Formulas, definitions, equations
avoidWhen: A formula transformed over several steps: use FormulaSteps
A small symbol inside a sentence: write $…$ in the text

props.name: tex
props.description: LaTeX formula. In a JSX attribute (tex="…") write \ once; in a JS string use String.raw`…`

props.name: at
props.description: Time: seconds, "cue:<phrase from the narration>", "cue:<phrase>@end", or "end-<seconds>"

props.name: size
props.description: Font size (px)

props.name: reveal
props.description: fade: fades in; write: appears left to right as if being written

props.name: duration
props.description: Time to appear (seconds); 0.7 for fade by default, by length for write

name: FormulaSteps
summary: Transforms a formula over several steps, each appearing with the narration.
useWhen: Proofs, simplifications, step-by-step calculations
avoidWhen: Only one formula: use Formula

props.name: steps
props.description: Transformation steps; each step replaces the previous one at `at`

props.name: keepPrevious
props.description: Keep earlier steps (dimmed) above instead of replacing them

name: MathMorph
summary: Equation rewriting by "matching symbols": the formula is split into pieces, pieces present in both steps slide to their new place (moving a term across, factoring out), new pieces appear, removed ones fade out.
useWhen: Solving an equation step by step: moving terms across, multiplying both sides, simplifying
Algebra where the viewer needs to see where each term goes
avoidWhen: A formula on its own: use Formula
Steps with nothing in common: use FormulaSteps

props.name: steps
props.type: { at: number | string; tokens: string | { tex: string; key?: string; color?: Color }[] }[]
props.description: Each step is one line of the formula split into pieces. Pieces with the same TeX (or the same key) in two steps slide to their new place

props.name: duration
props.description: Duration of each transformation (seconds)

props.name: spacing
props.description: Extra space between pieces (em)

name: Derivation
summary: A multi-line solution aligned on "=" (with &): each line is written with the narration, its reason on the right; earlier lines dim, the final answer is framed.
useWhen: Multi-step problems: solving equations, proofs, integrals, physics / chemistry exercises
When viewers need the earlier steps on screen to compare
avoidWhen: To see each term move: use MathMorph
One formula: use Formula

props.name: lines
props.type: { tex: string; at: number | string; note?: string; tone?: Color; result?: boolean }[]

props.name: dim
props.description: Dim earlier lines so the eye follows the new one

name: Axes
summary: A coordinate system holding math objects placed by coordinates (Plot, Point, Vector, Segment, Polygon, Circle, AreaUnder, Riemann, Tangent, VectorField, Angle, Label). `view` zooms/pans into a region and `matrix` transforms the whole plane.
useWhen: Functions, several curves, points moving on a graph, sliding tangents, areas, Riemann sums
Vectors, linear transformations, determinants (grid="plane" + matrix + basis)
Plane geometry with coordinates: triangles, circles, angles (axes={false} grid="none")
Zooming into a point to see the curve become almost straight (view)
avoidWhen: Block diagrams, processes: use Diagram
Statistics: use BarChart
children: Coordinate objects only (Plot, Point, Vector, Segment, Polygon, Circle, AreaUnder, Riemann, Tangent, VectorField, Angle, Label)

props.name: x
props.description: x range shown [min, max]

props.name: y
props.description: y range; when empty it is chosen so 1 x unit = 1 y unit, centered on 0

props.name: at
props.description: When the axes appear (they draw out from the origin)

props.name: axes
props.description: Draw the two axes; false for pure geometry (shapes only, no axes)

props.name: grid
props.description: subtle: faint grid; plane: clear blue coordinate plane (linear algebra); none

props.name: ticks
props.description: Numbers on the axes

props.name: tickStep
props.description: Tick step [x, y]; leave empty to choose automatically

props.name: labels
props.description: Axis names, support $…$

props.name: equal
props.description: Keep 1 x unit = 1 y unit (circles look round); the box shrinks to keep the ratio

props.name: view
props.type: { at: number | string; x: [number, number]; y: [number, number] }[]
props.description: Math camera: at `at` the view window glides to a new x, y range (zoom into a point on a curve, zoom back out)

props.name: matrix
props.type: { at: number | string; m: [[number, number], [number, number]] }[]
props.description: Linear transformation of the whole plane: grid, vectors, points and shapes all follow. Each key is relative to the original matrix, not cumulative

props.name: basis
props.description: Show the basis vectors î (ok) and ĵ (err), following `matrix`

props.name: warp
props.type: { at: number | string; fx: string; fy: string }[]
props.description: NONLINEAR transformation of the whole plane: the point (x, y) goes to (fx, fy) and the grid bends with it. Complex map w = z²: { fx: "x^2 - y^2", fy: "2*x*y" }. Each key is relative to the original plane

props.name: transition
props.description: Duration of each view/matrix change (seconds)

name: Stage
summary: A free stage (no axes, 1 x unit = 1 y unit, 16 × 9 units by default, origin in the center) for BUILDING PICTURES in any subject: place shapes by coordinates (Polygon, Circle, Path, Region, Spring, Vector, Segment, Point, Label), move them with Group / time, zoom with `view`.
useWhen: Physics: inclined planes, pendulums, springs, forces (Vector), light through lenses, planetary orbits
Biology / geography: hand-drawn pictures (cells, leaves, rivers, simplified maps, wind directions) with Path, Circle, Label
Geometry without axes; a situation with concrete positions
avoidWhen: Block diagrams with arrows: use Diagram (lays itself out)
Function graphs: use Axes
children: Coordinate objects as in Axes (including Group)

props.name: x
props.description: Horizontal coordinate range; 16 units by default

props.name: y
props.description: Vertical coordinate range; 9 units by default (16:9)

props.name: at
props.description: Time: seconds, "cue:<phrase from the narration>", "cue:<phrase>@end", or "end-<seconds>"

props.name: grid
props.description: Show a faint grid

props.name: view
props.type: { at: number | string; x: [number, number]; y: [number, number] }[]
props.description: Math camera: at `at` the view window glides to a new x, y range (zoom into a point on a curve, zoom back out)

props.name: transition
props.description: Duration of each view/matrix change (seconds)

name: Axes3D
summary: 3D space seen through a camera that can orbit (`azimuth`, `elevation` by keyframes, `spin` turns by itself). Holds Surface, Curve3D, Point3D, Vector3D, Segment3D, Solid.
useWhen: Solid geometry: pyramids, prisms, boxes (Solid, equal); hidden edges are dashed automatically
Functions of two variables z = f(x, y), surfaces, saddle points, extrema (Surface)
Vectors in space, space curves (helices), 3D trajectories
avoidWhen: Everything lies in one plane: a 2D Axes is clearer
children: 3D objects only (Surface, Curve3D, Point3D, Vector3D, Segment3D, Solid)

props.name: at
props.description: Time: seconds, "cue:<phrase from the narration>", "cue:<phrase>@end", or "end-<seconds>"

props.name: equal
props.description: The same scale on all three axes (REQUIRED for solid geometry so shapes are not distorted); false: each axis fits the box (surfaces, graphs)

props.name: azimuth
props.type: number | { at: number | string; value: number; duration?: number; ease?: "smooth" | "linear" | "spring" }[]
props.description: Camera rotation around the z axis (degrees); keyframes to orbit

props.name: elevation
props.type: number | { at: number | string; value: number; duration?: number; ease?: "smooth" | "linear" | "spring" }[]
props.description: Camera elevation above the xy plane (degrees, -80…80)

props.name: spin
props.description: Steady rotation around the z axis, degrees per second (e.g. 8), so the viewer feels the depth

props.name: zoom
props.type: number | { at: number | string; value: number; duration?: number; ease?: "smooth" | "linear" | "spring" }[]
props.description: A fixed number, or keyframes [{ at: 0, value: 1 }, { at: "cue:…", value: 3 }]: the first key is the starting value, each later key moves smoothly to its value

props.name: axes
props.description: Draw the three axes x, y, z

props.name: floor
props.description: Faint grid on the plane z = 0 (or the floor of the box)

name: Graph
summary: A function plot with axes and grid: the curve draws itself, moving tangents/secants, points and shaded areas.
useWhen: Functions, slope, derivatives, extrema, integrals
A secant sliding into a tangent
avoidWhen: Statistical data charts
Plane geometry or diagrams: use Diagram

props.name: fn
props.description: Expression in x: "x^2", "sin(x)", "2x+1", "sqrt(x)"; supports sin cos tan sqrt abs exp ln log pi e

props.name: domain
props.description: x range shown

props.name: range
props.description: y range; leave empty to compute it

props.name: at
props.description: When the axes appear

props.name: draw
props.description: When the curve starts drawing (defaults to at)

props.name: label
props.description: Curve label, e.g. "y = x²"

props.name: tangent
props.type: { x: number; to?: number; at?: number | string; moveAt?: number | string; moveDuration?: number }
props.description: Tangent at x, can slide to `to`

props.name: secant
props.type: { x1: number; x2: number; at?: number | string; shrinkAt?: number | string; shrinkTo?: number; shrinkDuration?: number; becomesTangentColor?: Color }
props.description: Secant through two points; the second point can slide to the first to illustrate the derivative

props.name: points
props.type: { x: number; label?: string; at?: number | string; color?: Color }[]

props.name: showSlope
props.description: Show the slope of the tangent/secant

props.name: area
props.type: { from: number; to: number; at?: number | string; color?: Color }
props.description: Shade the area under the curve from `from` to `to`

name: NumberLine
summary: A number line with automatic ticks: points moving by keyframes, arc jumps (addition/subtraction, sequences), shaded intervals for solution sets, zooming into a region.
useWhen: Integers, addition and subtraction, absolute value
Solution sets of inequalities (closed/open endpoints)
Convergent sequences, zooming in around the limit
avoidWhen: When a y axis is needed: use Axes

props.name: range
props.description: Range shown [min, max]

props.name: step
props.description: Tick step; leave empty to choose automatically

props.name: at
props.description: Time: seconds, "cue:<phrase from the narration>", "cue:<phrase>@end", or "end-<seconds>"

props.name: ticks
props.description: Show numbers under the ticks

props.name: view
props.description: Zoom/pan the number line to a new range at `at` (e.g. zoom in around √2)

props.name: points
props.type: { x: number | { at: number | string; value: number; duration?: number; ease?: "smooth" | "linear" | "spring" }[]; label?: string; color?: Color; at?: number | string }[]

props.name: jumps
props.type: { from: number; to: number; at: number | string; label?: string; color?: Color }[]
props.description: An arc jump from `from` to `to` (addition, subtraction, sequences)

props.name: intervals
props.type: { from: number; to: number; at?: number | string; color?: Color; closed?: [boolean, boolean]; label?: string }[]
props.description: A highlighted interval on the line (solution set of an inequality)

name: ArrayViz
summary: An array of cells driven step by step, animated: swaps (two cells arc around each other), inserts, writes, compared cells lifting, i/j pointers sliding, pivot, current range, region brackets, splitting into chunks (divide and conquer), cells bouncing when placed. Computes every position itself, text never overlaps.
useWhen: Algorithms on arrays: sorting (quick, merge, insertion, bubble), binary search, two pointers, sliding window
Step-by-step simulation, one step per narration sentence
avoidWhen: More than 16 elements
More than ~10 steps in one scene: split the scene; the next scene starts from the previous end state (pass the new values)

props.name: values
props.description: Initial values, at most 16 cells

props.name: steps
props.type: { at: number | string; swap?: [integer, integer]; move?: [integer, integer]; set?: { index: integer; value: number | string }[]; pointers?: object; compare?: integer[]; pivot?: integer | null; done?: integer[]; range?: [integer, integer] | null; regions?: { from: integer; to: integer; label?: string; tone?: Color }[]; note?: string; split?: integer[] }[]
props.description: Steps in time order

props.name: at
props.description: When the array appears

props.name: label
props.description: Array name shown on the left, e.g. "A"

props.name: pointerTones
props.description: Color of each pointer, e.g. { i: "ok", j: "info" }

props.name: width
props.description: Maximum width (px)

props.name: transition
props.description: Duration of each step's motion (seconds)

name: Tree
summary: A tree that lays itself out (just declare parents): recursion trees, binary trees, classification trees. Nodes grow in, edges draw themselves; `visit` makes nodes bounce and light up in traversal order.
useWhen: Recursion trees of quick sort / merge sort / Fibonacci
Binary search trees, heaps, decision trees
avoidWhen: Graphs with cycles or several parents: use Diagram
More than ~20 nodes

props.name: nodes
props.type: { id: string; label: string; parent: string | null; at?: number | string; tone?: Color; toneAt?: number | string }[]

props.name: at
props.description: Default time; nodes without `at` appear in traversal order, `gap` apart

props.name: size
props.description: Maximum font size in a node (shrinks when tight)

props.name: visit
props.type: { id: string; at: number | string; tone?: Color }[]
props.description: Traversal: nodes bounce and light up in turn (DFS, BFS, a search path). The node being visited has a glowing ring

name: Diagram
summary: Block diagram / discrete graph: nodes and arrows draw themselves in turn; `pulses` send a bright dot along edges, `highlights` recolor nodes with the narration (BFS, Dijkstra, data flow).
useWhen: Processes, cause → effect chains
Graphs in algorithms (Dijkstra, BFS)
Concept maps
avoidWhen: Function graphs: use Graph
More than 10 nodes: split the scene

props.name: nodes
props.type: { id: string; label: string; x: number; y: number; at?: number | string; tone?: Color; shape?: "box" | "circle" }[]

props.name: edges
props.type: { from: string; to: string; label?: string; at?: number | string; tone?: Color; directed?: boolean }[]

props.name: pulses
props.type: { from: string; to: string; at: number | string; tone?: Color; duration?: number }[]
props.description: A bright dot travelling along the edge from→to at time at: data/signal passing through, a BFS/DFS step

props.name: highlights
props.type: { id: string; at: number | string; tone?: Color }[]
props.description: Recolor a node's outline at time at (with a small bounce). The node keeps the color until changed again

props.name: at
props.description: Default time for nodes/edges without `at`

props.name: gap
props.description: Delay between nodes appearing one by one

props.name: nodeSize
props.description: Font size in the nodes

name: BarChart
summary: A bar chart that grows in; with `steps` bars swap (sliding past each other), change height, lift when compared, turn green when done: sorting shown with bars.
useWhen: Comparing quantities, running times, numbers of comparisons
Sorting algorithms shown with bar heights (bubble, selection, insertion)
Values changing over time
avoidWhen: A continuous function: use Graph
More than 16 bars
When i/j pointers and indices are needed: use ArrayViz

props.name: bars
props.type: { label: string; value: number; tone?: Color; at?: number | string; valueLabel?: string }[]

props.name: at
props.description: When the first bar grows (bars without `at` follow `gap` apart)

props.name: steps
props.type: { at: number | string; swap?: [integer, integer]; set?: { index: integer; value: number }[]; compare?: integer[]; done?: integer[]; tone?: { index: integer; tone: Color }[] }[]
props.description: Steps in time: swap, change height, compare, mark done

props.name: max
props.description: Value at full height; the largest value by default

props.name: unit
props.description: Unit written after the number, e.g. " ms"

name: Table
summary: Comparison table: column headers, rows appear one by one, one row can be highlighted.
useWhen: Comparing several options on a few criteria (complexity, stability, memory)
A table of x and f(x) values
avoidWhen: More than 8 rows or 6 columns: split the scene
Cells with long sentences: use Cards

props.name: columns
props.description: Column header, supports $…$

props.name: rows
props.type: { cells: string[]; at?: number | string; tone?: Color; toneAt?: number | string }[]

props.name: at
props.description: When the table (column headers) appears; rows without `at` follow `gap` apart

props.name: size
props.description: Font size in the cells

name: Cards
summary: 2–4 cards side by side, each with a name and a few short points; cards can be highlighted in turn.
useWhen: Comparing 2–4 options, variants or strategies (Lomuto vs Hoare, pivot choices)
Pros and cons
avoidWhen: Just one list of points: use BulletReveal
Comparing many criteria in a grid: use Table

props.name: cards
props.type: { title: string; points?: string[]; tone?: Color; at?: number | string }[]

props.name: at
props.description: Time: seconds, "cue:<phrase from the narration>", "cue:<phrase>@end", or "end-<seconds>"

props.name: gap
props.description: Delay between cards appearing (seconds)

props.name: focus
props.description: Highlight one card at a time (the others dim) at these moments

props.name: width
props.description: Width (px); fills the container by default. Cards wrap when tight

name: DotGrid
summary: A grid of dots (or squares) to count and talk about probability: groups are colored one by one with the narration, with counts.
useWhen: Probability, "1 in 100" rates, Bayes' theorem, false positives
Percentages, fractions you can see, sample spaces
avoidWhen: Comparing large numbers between groups: use BarChart

props.name: count
props.description: Total number of dots (e.g. 100 people)

props.name: cols
props.description: Number of columns; leave empty to choose automatically

props.name: size
props.description: Size of each dot (px); chosen from the count by default

props.name: at
props.description: When the dots appear (spreading in)

props.name: groups
props.type: { count: integer; color: Color; at: number | string; label?: string }[]
props.description: Color in turn: each group colors the next `count` dots at `at`. E.g. 1 sick person in 100

props.name: legend
props.description: Show a legend of the groups (label + count) below

name: Callout
summary: A highlighted note box: definition, caution, tip, common mistake.
useWhen: A short definition to remember
Warning about a common mistake
avoidWhen: The main content of a long scene: use BulletReveal

props.name: text
props.description: Content, supports $…$

props.name: at
props.description: Time: seconds, "cue:<phrase from the narration>", "cue:<phrase>@end", or "end-<seconds>"

name: CodeBlock
summary: A code block with line numbers: lines appear one by one, important lines are highlighted.
useWhen: Programming and algorithm lectures
avoidWhen: Math formulas: use Formula
More than 18 lines: trim or split the scene

props.name: title
props.description: File name shown above

props.name: at
props.description: Time: seconds, "cue:<phrase from the narration>", "cue:<phrase>@end", or "end-<seconds>"

props.name: lineGap
props.description: Seconds between lines appearing; 0 to show all at once

props.name: highlight
props.description: Lines (counting from 1) to highlight

props.name: highlightAt
props.description: When the highlight starts

props.name: steps
props.description: Move the highlight with the narration: [{ at, highlight: [3] }, { at, highlight: [8] }]. Use this instead of several CodeBlocks

name: Timeline
summary: Horizontal timeline: events appear one by one with the narration, labels alternate above/below, with icons; `focus` highlights one event.
useWhen: History: the course of events, dynasties, campaigns
An author's life, the history of an invention, stages of development
avoidWhen: Steps of a process not tied to dates: use Diagram or Cycle

name: Cycle
summary: A cycle: stages (with icons) around a circle, curved arrows from one to the next, a dot travelling around; `active` highlights the stage being discussed.

Geography: water cycle, rock cycle
Economics, society: feedback loops
avoidWhen: A process with a start and an end: use Diagram
